# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 22/12/2025

## 🔥 Top Stories
- Researchers from Southwest Jiaotong University, China, have introduced a novel object detection pipeline called JMM-Net, designed to operate effectively in murky, turbid water.
- The JMM-Net system incorporates two key components: a Multi-Scale Channel Attention (MSCA) module and a Multi-Perception Head (MPPhead) to improve detection of small, faint, or overlapping objects.
- The researchers also propose a lightweight neck structure called GS-PAN, which reduces computational cost while maintaining multi-scale fusion capability.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- The JMM-Net system modifies the YOLOX model by adding MSCA to the backbone network and MPPhead as the detection head, enhancing sensitivity to subtle color and texture cues.
- The MSCA module uses Local-Global Channel Attention (LGCA) and Context-based Cross-Channel Attention (C3A) to selectively amplify useful channels and suppress uninformative ones.
- The MPPhead introduces Inner Layer Attention (ILA) for scale perception, Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA), Deformable Convolution with Batch Normalization and Activation (DCBS) for spatial perception, and Task Cooperation Attention (TCA) for task perception.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- The GS-PAN neck structure uses Group Shuffle Convolution (GSConv) to reduce computational cost while maintaining multi-scale fusion capability, making it a valuable contribution to the field of underwater object detection.

## 📰 Industry News
- The introduction of JMM-Net highlights the importance of handling low-quality imagery with limited computational resources, particularly in the field of underwater object detection.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- The full paper on Joint Multi-Scale Channel Attention and Multi-Perception Head for Underwater Object Detection is available for download: https://journalclub.io/track/7bFDcRTLuEUM7dp7aHIeQfQZ94VygmgLERTyDaT9gtYAxbwJsN

## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from Southwest Jiaotong University, China, have introduced a novel object detection pipeline, JMM-Net, designed to operate effectively in murky, turbid water.
- The JMM-Net system incorporates two key components: a Multi-Scale Channel Attention (MSCA) module to enhance the model's sensitivity to subtle color and texture cues, and a Multi-Perception Head (MPPhead) to improve recognition of small, faint, or overlapping objects.
- The MSCA module uses Local-Global Channel Attention (LGCA) and Context-based Cross-Channel Attention (C3A) to selectively amplify useful channels and suppress uninformative ones.
- MPPhead introduces Inner Layer Attention (ILA) for scale perception, Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) and Deformable Convolution with Batch Normalization and Activation (DCBS) for spatial perception, and Task Cooperation Attention (TCA) for task perception.
- The researchers also propose GS-PAN, a lightweight neck structure using Group Shuffle Convolution (GSConv) to reduce computational cost while maintaining multi-scale fusion capability.

### Detailed Points
- The newsletter discusses the challenges of underwater object detection, including refraction and light degradation, which affect the accuracy of traditional object detection models.
- The authors modify the YOLOX model by adding MSCA to the backbone network and MPPhead as the detection head.
- MSCA has two sub-modules: LGCA, which captures local and global channel dependencies, and C3A, which fuses the two streams together using cross-channel information aggregation and self-attention pooling.
- MPPhead combines scale perception through ILA, spatial perception through EMA and DCBS, and task perception through TCA to handle scale variations, irregular shapes, and complex backgrounds in underwater scenes.
- The GS-PAN neck structure replaces standard convolutions with GSConv, a lightweight convolution technique that combines the efficiency of depthwise separable convolutions with the representational power of standard convolutions.
- The researchers test their new invention and provide benchmarking results, which are available in the full paper.
- The newsletter highlights the importance of handling low-quality imagery with limited computational resources, making the JMM-Net system a valuable contribution to the field of underwater object detection.

Joint Multi-Scale Channel Attention and Multi-Perception Head for Underwater Object Detection   

Imagine that you’re at a lake, standing on a boat dock. You’re filming some fish swimming by when your phone slips out of your hand. It hits the ground, bounces off the wood, and…plunk…it’s in the water. Uh oh. Before you can react, it’s already slipped beneath the surface. The screen is still on (and glowing), but the water is murky. So as the phone sinks to the bottom, the whole thing disappears from sight.

![](https://journalclub.io/px/rpMEzmSAsxqpyDwIcvEIlgsOOmuuU3VZZ7xaEmAZ8fKyibxbsn)

Joint Multi-Scale Channel Attention and Multi-Perception Head for Underwater Object Detection
